text: {"score":4,"justification":"The summary is accurate, cautious and grounded. The headline, share, expected share, risk-adjusted score, z-score, 9% low-complexity share, 18 documented claims, 1 of 5 (20%) below billed, 15% comparison rate and 0 of 16 all match the card. The claim that rates run above the all-provider rate in every band from 1 condition upward is true (0.064>0.035 through 0.429>0.3). It flags the thin records and gives concrete chart-request steps. The weaknesses are a headline that overstates ('every complexity band' when band 0 is 0.023 vs 0.021), a misleading sentence about cloned notes, and next steps that are less specific than the prose.","problems":["Headline says 'elevated rates in every complexity band' but the 0-condition band is only marginally higher (0.023 vs 0.021); the body correctly says 'from 1 condition upward'.","'0 of 16 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data reviewed had no lab or test line' is awkward, and 'no sign of cloned notes' overreaches: a lab line on the claim does not rule out cloning.","Says 'most of this provider's 99215s fall on patients with 3 or more conditions' without a number. By the card, 274 of 353 is about 78%, derivable but not stated.","The formal next_steps are generic (larger sample, re-screen) and omit the specific claims named in the prose (C0005324, C0006268, C0007454, C0007603).","The example C0005941 (documented moderate MDM) is the only documentation example, and the summary does not note that it is a single case. The 99215 number flag is a false alarm (the CPT code).","The citation of C0007389 and C0006041 as 'plausible high-MDM' is only a plausibility read on diagnoses and conditions, since no documentation was returned for them."]}
